title: A Pedagogical Introduction to Anomalies in Quantum Field Theory
summary: These notes are aimed at providing a relatively concise and self-contained introduction to anomalies in quantum field theory. A first part reviews the necessary notions of quantum field theory, in particular its functional integral formulation which we use throughout. Then we discuss in some detail how and why anomalies arise as non-invariance of the functional integral measure or through the absence of a regulator preserving all symmetries, and how they manifest themselves as current non-conservation in anomalous loop diagrams and anomalous Ward identities, or equivalently as a non-invariance of the effective action. Specifically, we deal with the so-called abelian anomaly under chiral transformations, and the so-called chiral anomaly which is a violation of non-abelian gauge invariance in the presence of chiral fermions. We perform a detailed triangle Feynman diagram computation for both cases. Then we move on to provide a brief overview of some important properties of anomalies (locality, finiteness, one-loop exactness), and how they are characterized in general by the Wess-Zumino consistency condition. We show how this condition can be reformulated in terms of BRST cohomology and how it can be solved, for arbitrary (even) space-time dimensions, by the descent equations. Finally, we briefly discuss the general relation between anomalies in arbitrary even dimensions 2n and index theorems in 2n+2 dimensions, generalizing also to gravitational anomalies. We conclude with the exhibition of the highly non-trivial anomaly cancellation in ten-dimensional IIB supergravity.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a concise, self-contained introduction to quantum field theory anomalies, covering their origin in functional integral non-invariance or regulator limitations, manifestations (e.g., current non-conservation, anomalous Ward identities, effective action non-invariance), explicit triangle diagram computations for abelian and chiral anomalies, key properties (locality, finiteness, one-loop exactness), the Wess-Zumino consistency condition and its BRST/cohomological formulation via descent equations, connections to index theorems in higher dimensions, gravitational anomalies, and anomaly cancellation in 10D IIB supergravity.
AI.motivation: To offer a pedagogical, unified, and rigorous exposition of anomalies—bridging conceptual foundations, computational techniques (e.g., triangle diagrams), cohomological classification (Wess-Zumino, BRST, descent), and physical implications (e.g., anomaly cancellation in string-theoretic gravity).
AI.method: Functional integral formulation of QFT; explicit perturbative computation of triangle Feynman diagrams; analysis of symmetry breaking in regularization; derivation and solution of the Wess-Zumino consistency condition using BRST cohomology and descent equations; dimensional generalization linking anomalies in 2n dimensions to index theorems in 2n+2 dimensions; application to gravitational and mixed anomalies.
AI.result: Systematic derivation and classification of abelian (chiral) and non-abelian chiral anomalies; proof of locality, finiteness, and one-loop exactness; cohomological characterization via BRST-invariant descent solutions; general correspondence between anomalies and index theorems; explicit verification of anomaly cancellation in ten-dimensional type IIB supergravity.
AI.conclusion: Anomalies are robust, topological obstructions to symmetry preservation in quantum field theory, fully characterized by cohomology and deeply connected to geometry (index theorems); their consistent cancellation—exemplified in IIB supergravity—is essential for quantum consistency of fundamental theories.
